key_insight: The paper shows that ensemble Kalman inversion can tune a 16-parameter spectral eddy viscosity closure online to better match LES energy spectra to DNS in forced 2D turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This offers a derivative-free route to calibrate subgrid-scale models for LES, improving predictive fidelity without hand-tuning closure coefficients.
method: Parameterize a wavenumber-dependent eddy viscosity with 16 unknowns.
Run an ensemble of coarse LES simulations and compare their kinetic energy spectra to DNS.
Iteratively update the parameters with ensemble Kalman inversion to reduce spectral mismatch.
evidence_signal: The closure is evaluated by comparing LES and filtered DNS kinetic energy spectra up to the resolved wavenumber range, with convergence of the spectral mismatch used as the main accuracy indicator.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated for forced two-dimensional turbulence, so robustness and transferability to other flows, Reynolds numbers, or 3D turbulence remain to be validated.
paper_title: Online Learning of a Spectral Eddy Viscosity Closure for Large Eddy Simulation Using Ensemble Kalman Inversion
